name: European Coal and Steel Community (1958–1973)
description: Two equal horizontal stripes of blue over black, each bearing three yellow five-pointed stars in a row — one star for each of the six founding member states.
history: The ECSC flag was adopted in 1958. Blue stands for steel and black for coal; the number of stars was raised with each enlargement (nine in 1973, ten in 1981, twelve in 1986) until the ECSC treaty expired in 2002. This is the original six-star version.
